claim: Rps27 and Rps27l likely arose during whole-genome duplication(s) in a common vertebrate ancestor.
source: Evolutionary analysis suggests that Rps27 and Rps27l likely arose during whole-genome duplication(s) in a common vertebrate ancestor.
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis showing Rps27 paralogs present in vertebrates but not invertebrates, synteny analysis, and timing coinciding with known whole-genome duplications.

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l have inversely correlated mRNA abundance across mouse cell types.
source: We show that Rps27 and Rps27l have inversely correlated mRNA abundance across mouse cell types, with the highest Rps27 in lymphocytes and the highest Rps27l in mammary alveolar cells and hepatocytes.
evidence: Demonstrated through analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data from Mouse Cell Atlas and other datasets, showing negative correlation (Pearson's r = -0.58, p=4.4e-09).

claim: The highest Rps27 expression is in lymphocytes.
source: We show that Rps27 and Rps27l have inversely correlated mRNA abundance across mouse cell types, with the highest Rps27 in lymphocytes and the highest Rps27l in mammary alveolar cells and hepatocytes.
evidence: Shown in single-cell RNA-seq analysis from Mouse Cell Atlas.

claim: The highest Rps27l expression is in mammary alveolar cells and hepatocytes.
source: We show that Rps27 and Rps27l have inversely correlated mRNA abundance across mouse cell types, with the highest Rps27 in lymphocytes and the highest Rps27l in mammary alveolar cells and hepatocytes.
evidence: Shown in single-cell RNA-seq analysis from Mouse Cell Atlas and confirmed by RT-qPCR.

claim: Rps27- and Rps27l-ribosomes associate preferentially with different transcripts.
source: By endogenously tagging the Rps27 and Rps27l proteins, we demonstrate that Rps27- and Rps27l-ribosomes associate preferentially with different transcripts.
evidence: Demonstrated through FLAG-IP ribosome profiling experiments showing differential enrichment of specific transcripts.

claim: Murine Rps27 and Rps27l loss-of-function alleles are homozygous lethal at different developmental stages.
source: Furthermore, murine Rps27 and Rps27l loss-of-function alleles are homozygous lethal at different developmental stages.
evidence: Demonstrated through generation and breeding of Rps27exon2del and Rps27lexon2del mice, showing early embryonic lethality for Rps27 and postnatal lethality for Rps27l.

claim: Expressing Rps27 protein from the endogenous Rps27l locus completely rescues loss-of-function lethality.
source: However, strikingly, expressing Rps27 protein from the endogenous Rps27l locus or vice versa completely rescues loss-of-function lethality and yields mice with no detectable deficits.
evidence: Demonstrated through generation of Rps27lRps27 mice that are viable and fertile with normal genotype ratios.

claim: Expressing Rps27l protein from the endogenous Rps27 locus completely rescues loss-of-function lethality.
source: However, strikingly, expressing Rps27 protein from the endogenous Rps27l locus or vice versa completely rescues loss-of-function lethality and yields mice with no detectable deficits.
evidence: Demonstrated through generation of Rps27Rps27l mice that are viable and fertile with normal genotype ratios.

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are evolutionarily retained because their subfunctionalized expression patterns render both genes necessary to achieve the requisite total expression of two equivalent proteins across cell types.
source: Together, these findings suggest that Rps27 and Rps27l are evolutionarily retained because their subfunctionalized expression patterns render both genes necessary to achieve the requisite total expression of two equivalent proteins across cell types.
evidence: Inferred from the combination of inverse expression patterns, complete rescue by protein swapping, and lack of detectable phenotypes in homogenized mice.

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l proteins differ by only three N-terminal residues out of 84 total residues.
source: Notably, while the coding sequences of Rps27 and Rps27l are highly divergent, almost all substitutions are synonymous and their protein sequences only differ by three N-terminal residues out of a total of 84: K5R, P12L, and R17K.
evidence: Determined through sequence alignment of Rps27 and Rps27l proteins.

claim: The three differing residues between Rps27 and Rps27l are K5R, P12L, and R17K.
source: Notably, while the coding sequences of Rps27 and Rps27l are highly divergent, almost all substitutions are synonymous and their protein sequences only differ by three N-terminal residues out of a total of 84: K5R, P12L, and R17K.
evidence: Determined through sequence alignment.

claim: The three differing residues between Rps27 and Rps27l are well-conserved among mammals.
source: These differences between the two paralogous proteins are well-conserved among mammals (Figure 1C).
evidence: Shown through multi-species protein sequence alignment in Figure 1C.

claim: None of the nine included invertebrate species had more than one Rps27 ortholog.
source: While none of the nine included invertebrates had more than one Rps27 ortholog, nearly all vertebrates had two Rps27 paralogs, and most teleost fish species had three to six (Figure 1B).
evidence: Determined through phylogenetic analysis of Rps27 orthologs across species.

claim: Nearly all vertebrates had two Rps27 paralogs.
source: While none of the nine included invertebrates had more than one Rps27 ortholog, nearly all vertebrates had two Rps27 paralogs, and most teleost fish species had three to six (Figure 1B).
evidence: Determined through phylogenetic analysis of Rps27 orthologs across species.

claim: Most teleost fish species had three to six Rps27 paralogs.
source: While none of the nine included invertebrates had more than one Rps27 ortholog, nearly all vertebrates had two Rps27 paralogs, and most teleost fish species had three to six (Figure 1B).
evidence: Determined through phylogenetic analysis of Rps27 orthologs across species.

claim: The Rps27l locus is flanked by several other genes that also have paralogs near the Rps27 locus and are arranged in similar order.
source: Furthermore, the Rps27l locus is flanked by several other genes that also have paralogs near the Rps27 locus and are arranged in similar order (Figure 1A).
evidence: Shown through synteny analysis of genomic regions around Rps27 and Rps27l loci.

claim: The syntenic genomic regions containing Rps27 and Rps27l likely originated via DNA-based duplication.
source: Thus, these syntenic genomic regions likely originated via DNA-based duplication.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of introns, synteny, and absence of hallmarks of retrotransposition.

claim: Rps27l mRNA levels increase in luminal cells between pregnancy and lactation.
source: We found that Rps27l mRNA levels increase in luminal cells between pregnancy and lactation, while Rps27 mRNA levels diminish (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Shown through analysis of bulk RNA-seq data from sorted mammary cell types.

claim: Rps27 mRNA levels diminish in luminal cells between pregnancy and lactation.
source: We found that Rps27l mRNA levels increase in luminal cells between pregnancy and lactation, while Rps27 mRNA levels diminish (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Shown through analysis of bulk RNA-seq data from sorted mammary cell types.

claim: Among mature alveolar cells, single cells expressing the highest levels of milk protein transcripts such as Csn2 and Wap also had the highest Rps27l expression.
source: Among mature alveolar cells, single cells expressing the highest levels of milk protein transcripts such as Csn2 and Wap also had the highest Rps27l expression (Figure 1E).
evidence: Shown through correlation analysis in single-cell RNA-seq data (Csn2: Spearman's ρ = 0.63, p=5.7e-13; Wap: Spearman's ρ = 0.56, p=6.7e-10).

claim: Rps27l is transcriptionally upregulated by Trp53 via two Trp53-binding elements within the Rps27l genomic locus.
source: It has previously been reported that Rps27l is transcriptionally upregulated by Trp53 via two Trp53-binding elements within the Rps27l genomic locus, and that Trp53 also downregulates Rps27 expression (He and Sun, 2007; Li et al., 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (He and Sun, 2007; Li et al., 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Trp53 downregulates Rps27 expression.
source: It has previously been reported that Rps27l is transcriptionally upregulated by Trp53 via two Trp53-binding elements within the Rps27l genomic locus, and that Trp53 also downregulates Rps27 expression (He and Sun, 2007; Li et al., 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (He and Sun, 2007; Li et al., 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Differences in Rps27 and Rps27l expression across cell types are not primarily driven by Trp53 activity.
source: These findings, therefore, suggest that differences in Rps27 and Rps27l expression across cell types are not primarily driven by Trp53 activity.
evidence: Inferred from RT-qPCR data showing Trp53 mRNA levels do not correlate with Rps27/Rps27l changes during mammary development, and single-cell data showing inverse correlation between Rps27l and other Trp53 targets.

claim: Both Rps27 and Rps27l are expressed in most tissues.
source: Previous work has shown that both Rps27 and Rps27l are expressed in most tissues and are incorporated into actively translating ribosomes (O'Donohue et al., 2010; Xiong et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (O'Donohue et al., 2010; Xiong et al., 2014).

claim: Both Rps27 and Rps27l are incorporated into actively translating ribosomes.
source: Previous work has shown that both Rps27 and Rps27l are expressed in most tissues and are incorporated into actively translating ribosomes (O'Donohue et al., 2010; Xiong et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (O'Donohue et al., 2010; Xiong et al., 2014) and confirmed by density gradient fractionation in this study.

claim: Homozygous Rps27l knockout is lethal at early postnatal stages with increased apoptosis in hematopoietic organs.
source: While no Rps27 knockout mouse has previously been described, homozygous Rps27l knockout is lethal at early postnatal stages with increased apoptosis in hematopoietic organs (Xiong et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Xiong et al., 2014).

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are differentially regulated upon activation of the tumor suppressor Trp53.
source: Rps27 and Rps27l are differentially regulated upon activation of the tumor suppressor Trp53 and have opposite feedback effects on the Trp53-Mdm2 axis (He and Sun, 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (He and Sun, 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l have opposite feedback effects on the Trp53-Mdm2 axis.
source: Rps27 and Rps27l are differentially regulated upon activation of the tumor suppressor Trp53 and have opposite feedback effects on the Trp53-Mdm2 axis (He and Sun, 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (He and Sun, 2007; Xiong et al., 2014; Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are detectable among fractions corresponding to actively translating ribosomes (polysomes).
source: Using antibodies specific to each paralog with only trace cross-reactivity to the other paralog (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), we found that Rps27 and Rps27l are both detectable among fractions corresponding to actively translating ribosomes (polysomes), fractions corresponding to single ribosomes (80S), and fractions representing the 40S small subunit.
evidence: Demonstrated through density gradient fractionation and western blot analysis.

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are detectable among fractions corresponding to single ribosomes (80S).
source: Using antibodies specific to each paralog with only trace cross-reactivity to the other paralog (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), we found that Rps27 and Rps27l are both detectable among fractions corresponding to actively translating ribosomes (polysomes), fractions corresponding to single ribosomes (80S), and fractions representing the 40S small subunit.
evidence: Demonstrated through density gradient fractionation and western blot analysis.

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are detectable among fractions representing the 40S small subunit.
source: Using antibodies specific to each paralog with only trace cross-reactivity to the other paralog (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), we found that Rps27 and Rps27l are both detectable among fractions corresponding to actively translating ribosomes (polysomes), fractions corresponding to single ribosomes (80S), and fractions representing the 40S small subunit.
evidence: Demonstrated through density gradient fractionation and western blot analysis.

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are not detectable in early fractions where most extra-ribosomal proteins are found.
source: Rps27 and Rps27l are not detectable in early fractions where most extra-ribosomal proteins are found (Figure 3A).
evidence: Demonstrated through density gradient fractionation and western blot analysis.

claim: In the structure of the human ribosome, the three paralog-specific amino acid positions of Rps27 are solvent-accessible.
source: In the structure of the human ribosome (Natchiar et al., 2017), Rps27 is incorporated into the 40S subunit such that the three paralog-specific amino acid positions are solvent-accessible (Figure 3B) and could modulate interactions with other molecules.
evidence: Based on analysis of published ribosome structure (Natchiar et al., 2017).

claim: The three paralog-specific amino acid positions of Rps27 could modulate interactions with other molecules.
source: In the structure of the human ribosome (Natchiar et al., 2017), Rps27 is incorporated into the 40S subunit such that the three paralog-specific amino acid positions are solvent-accessible (Figure 3B) and could modulate interactions with other molecules.
evidence: Speculated based on the solvent-accessible position of these residues in the ribosome structure.

claim: 8 transcripts were enriched among Rps27-ribosomes.
source: After excluding a Tmod3 transcript as a likely artifact of FLAG-IP (Appendix 1, Appendix 1—figure 1), we identified 8 transcripts enriched among Rps27-ribosomes and 46 transcripts enriched among Rps27l-ribosomes (absolute value of log2 fold change > 0.25, false discovery rate < 0.05; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Determined through ribosome profiling and statistical analysis.

claim: 46 transcripts were enriched among Rps27l-ribosomes.
source: After excluding a Tmod3 transcript as a likely artifact of FLAG-IP (Appendix 1, Appendix 1—figure 1), we identified 8 transcripts enriched among Rps27-ribosomes and 46 transcripts enriched among Rps27l-ribosomes (absolute value of log2 fold change > 0.25, false discovery rate < 0.05; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Determined through ribosome profiling and statistical analysis.

claim: Among transcripts enriched in Rps27l-ribosomes, Gene Ontology terms associated with cell cycle processes were enriched.
source: Among the latter set of transcripts, Gene Ontology terms associated with cell cycle processes were enriched (Figure 3G).
evidence: Determined through Gene Ontology enrichment analysis of differentially enriched transcripts.

claim: Rps27lexon2del/+ males and females are viable and fertile.
source: Similar to a previously described Rps27l gene-trapped loss-of-function mouse model (here termed Rps27lGT) (Xiong et al., 2014), Rps27lexon2del / + males and females are viable and fertile, but Rps27lexon2del / exon2del mice are observed at lower-than-expected frequencies in crosses of Rps27lexon2del / + males and females (Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments and genotype analysis.

claim: Rps27lexon2del/exon2del mice are observed at lower-than-expected frequencies in crosses of Rps27lexon2del/+ males and females.
source: Similar to a previously described Rps27l gene-trapped loss-of-function mouse model (here termed Rps27lGT) (Xiong et al., 2014), Rps27lexon2del / + males and females are viable and fertile, but Rps27lexon2del / exon2del mice are observed at lower-than-expected frequencies in crosses of Rps27lexon2del / + males and females (Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments and genotype analysis.

claim: Rps27lexon2del/exon2del offspring died or needed to be euthanized due to animal distress by postnatal days 13-17 (P13-17).
source: These Rps27lexon2del / exon2del offspring died or needed to be euthanized due to animal distress by postnatal days 13–17 (P13–17).
evidence: Observed through monitoring of offspring from breeding experiments.

claim: Rps27exon2del/+ mice are viable.
source: Interestingly, Rps27exon2del / + mice were also viable, but no Rps27exon2del / exon2del offspring were recovered from crosses of Rps27exon2del / + males and females (Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments and genotype analysis.

claim: No Rps27exon2del/exon2del offspring were recovered from crosses of Rps27exon2del/+ males and females.
source: Interestingly, Rps27exon2del / + mice were also viable, but no Rps27exon2del / exon2del offspring were recovered from crosses of Rps27exon2del / + males and females (Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments and genotype analysis.

claim: Only one Rps27exon2del/exon2del specimen out of 35 dissected embryos was recovered at embryonic day 8.5 (e8.5).
source: When we dissected embryonic day 8.5 (e8.5) embryos from Rps27exon2del / + × Rps27exon2del / + crosses, only one Rps27exon2del / exon2del specimen out of 35 dissected embryos was recovered.
evidence: Demonstrated through embryo dissection and genotyping.

claim: The Rps27exon2del/exon2del embryo recovered at e8.5 was severely delayed in development compared to littermates.
source: This Rps27exon2del / exon2del embryo was severely delayed in development compared to littermates (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: Observed through morphological examination of dissected embryos.

claim: Detectable protein expression from the Rps27 truncation allele is slightly diminished in Rps27exon2del/+ specimens.
source: For the Rps27 and Rps27l truncation allele genotypes that are viable at birth, we confirmed by western blot of multiple postnatal day 0 (P0) tissues that detectable protein expression from the respective truncated paralog is slightly diminished in Rps27exon2del / + specimens and nearly eliminated in Rps27lexon2del / exon2del specimens (Figure 4E and F), with residual detection due to trace antibody cross-reactivity against the intact paralog (as demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and D).
evidence: Demonstrated through western blot analysis of P0 tissues.

claim: Detectable protein expression from the Rps27l truncation allele is nearly eliminated in Rps27lexon2del/exon2del specimens.
source: For the Rps27 and Rps27l truncation allele genotypes that are viable at birth, we confirmed by western blot of multiple postnatal day 0 (P0) tissues that detectable protein expression from the respective truncated paralog is slightly diminished in Rps27exon2del / + specimens and nearly eliminated in Rps27lexon2del / exon2del specimens (Figure 4E and F), with residual detection due to trace antibody cross-reactivity against the intact paralog (as demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and D).
evidence: Demonstrated through western blot analysis of P0 tissues.

claim: Rps27lexon2del/+ and Rps27lexon2del/exon2del tissues had increased expression of the intact Rps27 protein.
source: Interestingly, we observed that Rps27lexon2del / + and Rps27lexon2del / exon2del tissues had increased expression of the intact Rps27 protein, which is analogous to previously reported instances in which depletion of an RP gene is associated with increased expression of a paralogous gene (Milenkovic et al., 2023; O'Leary et al., 2013).
evidence: Demonstrated through western blot analysis of P0 tissues.

claim: Impaired expression from the Rps27 locus impacts viability at significantly earlier embryonic stages than impaired expression from the Rps27l locus.
source: Together, these findings demonstrate that impaired expression from the Rps27 locus impacts viability at significantly earlier embryonic stages than impaired expression from the Rps27l locus.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of lethality timing between Rps27exon2del/exon2del (early embryonic) and Rps27lexon2del/exon2del (postnatal).

claim: The early postnatal lethality of Rps27lGT/GT can be rescued on a Trp53 loss-of-function background.
source: Previous work has shown that the early postnatal lethality of Rps27lGT/GT can be rescued on a Trp53 loss-of-function (Trp53LOF/+ or Trp53LOF/LOF) background.
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Xiong et al., 2014).

claim: Rps27lexon2del/exon2del;Trp53null/+ mice are viable.
source: We indeed found that Rps27lexon2del / exon2del;Trp53null / + mice are viable.
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments with Trp53null mice.

claim: No Rps27exon2del/exon2del;Trp53null/+ or Rps27exon2del/exon2del;Trp53null/null offspring were recovered from crossing Rps27exon2del/+;Trp53null/+ males and females.
source: However, no Rps27exon2del / exon2del;Trp53null / + or Rps27exon2del / exon2del;Trp53null / null offspring were recovered from crossing Rps27exon2del / +;Trp53null / + males and females (Figure 4G).
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments and genotype analysis.

claim: Disabling expression from the Rps27 locus disrupts ribosome biogenesis either to a greater degree than Rps27l that cannot be mitigated by Trp53 depletion or through a non-Trp53-mediated mechanism.
source: These results suggest that disabling expression from the Rps27 locus disrupts ribosome biogenesis either to a greater degree than Rps27l that cannot be mitigated by Trp53 depletion or through a non-Trp53-mediated mechanism.
evidence: Inferred from the inability of Trp53 loss to rescue Rps27exon2del/exon2del lethality.

claim: Heterozygous crosses for both Rps27Rps27l and Rps27lRps27 alleles resulted in normal genotype frequencies among offspring of both sexes.
source: Remarkably, heterozygous crosses for both alleles (Rps27Rps27l /+ × Rps27Rps27l /+, and Rps27lRps27 /+ × Rps27lRps27 /+) resulted in normal genotype frequencies among offspring of both sexes (Figure 5C).
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments and genotype analysis.

claim: Rps27Rps27l/Rps27l mice show loss of Rps27 protein and increased Rps27l protein.
source: Western blots of adult mouse tissues confirmed loss of Rps27 protein and increased Rps27l protein in Rps27Rps27l / Rps27l mice (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: Demonstrated through western blot analysis of adult tissues.

claim: The effect of Rps27 protein loss and Rps27l protein increase in Rps27Rps27l/Rps27l mice is most pronounced in the spleen.
source: This effect is most pronounced in the spleen, which contains abundant B cells, one of the cell types that highly express the Rps27 locus as shown above (Figure 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated through western blot analysis showing greatest change in spleen tissue.

claim: Rps27lRps27/Rps27 mice show loss of Rps27l protein expression with concurrently increased Rps27 protein.
source: Likewise, loss of Rps27l protein expression with concurrently increased Rps27 protein was observed in Rps27lRps27Rps27 / Rps27 mice (Figure 5D and E) and the effect is most pronounced in liver tissue, which contains hepatocytes that highly express the Rps27l locus (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Demonstrated through western blot analysis of adult tissues.

claim: The effect of Rps27l protein loss and Rps27 protein increase in Rps27lRps27/Rps27 mice is most pronounced in liver tissue.
source: Likewise, loss of Rps27l protein expression with concurrently increased Rps27 protein was observed in Rps27lRps27Rps27 / Rps27 mice (Figure 5D and E) and the effect is most pronounced in liver tissue, which contains hepatocytes that highly express the Rps27l locus (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Demonstrated through western blot analysis showing greatest change in liver tissue.

claim: Expressing Rps27 from the Rps27l locus completely rescues the early lethality observed upon homozygous truncation of Rps27l.
source: This demonstrates that expressing Rps27 from the Rps27l locus completely rescues the early lethality observed upon homozygous truncation of Rps27l, and vice versa.
evidence: Demonstrated through viability of Rps27lRps27/Rps27 mice.

claim: Expressing Rps27l from the Rps27 locus completely rescues the early lethality observed upon homozygous truncation of Rps27.
source: This demonstrates that expressing Rps27 from the Rps27l locus completely rescues the early lethality observed upon homozygous truncation of Rps27l, and vice versa.
evidence: Demonstrated through viability of Rps27Rps27l/Rps27l mice.

claim: Pups of all genotypes (including homogenized) gained weight at similar rates.
source: Later organism fitness was also rescued: pups of all genotypes gained weight at similar rates (Figure 5F), and male and female heterozygous and homozygous mice are viable to at least 1 year of age and are fertile.
evidence: Demonstrated through monitoring of pup weights at multiple timepoints.

claim: Male and female heterozygous and homozygous homogenized mice are viable to at least 1 year of age and are fertile.
source: Later organism fitness was also rescued: pups of all genotypes gained weight at similar rates (Figure 5F), and male and female heterozygous and homozygous mice are viable to at least 1 year of age and are fertile.
evidence: Demonstrated through long-term monitoring of mice.

claim: A detailed necropsy of homozygous 10-16-week-old males and age-matched wild-type controls revealed no clinically significant differences in gross organ weight, gross organ morphology, or tissue histology.
source: A detailed necropsy of homozygous 10–16-week-old males and age-matched wild-type controls, performed by a veterinary pathologist blinded to specimen genotype, revealed no clinically significant differences in gross organ weight, gross organ morphology, or tissue histology for either line (Supplementary file 4) upon examination of neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, lymphatic, endocrine, hematopoietic, integumentary, and musculoskeletal tissues.
evidence: Demonstrated through comprehensive necropsy performed by blinded veterinary pathologist.

claim: A liver panel and complete blood count performed on 10-16-week-old male necropsy specimens yielded no clinically significant differences between genotypes.
source: A liver panel and complete blood count were performed on the 10–16-week-old male necropsy specimens to survey for anomalies in liver function or hematopoiesis. These yielded no clinically significant differences between genotypes (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Demonstrated through bloodwork analysis.

claim: No statistically significant differences in pup weight gain were detected between any of the maternal genotypes in homogenized mice.
source: Since genetically manipulated mouse lines can exhibit lactation failure at a range of timepoints (Palmer et al., 2006), litter size and pup weight were assessed at P4, P13, and P21 (Figure 6B). No statistically significant differences in pup weight gain were detected between any of the maternal genotypes.
evidence: Demonstrated through monitoring of pup weights from dams of different genotypes.

claim: No anomalies in mammary gland morphogenesis were detected in homogenized mice.
source: We, therefore, used carmine alum staining and hematoxylin-eosin staining to assess the gross morphology and mammary fat pad filling of nulliparous, pregnant, and lactating females (Figure 6C). No anomalies in mammary gland morphogenesis were detected, with all genotypes exhibiting similar epithelial branch length and number, fat pad filling, alveolar size, and alveolar wall thickness.
evidence: Demonstrated through histological analysis of mammary glands.

claim: All genotypes of homogenized mice exhibited similar epithelial branch length and number, fat pad filling, alveolar size, and alveolar wall thickness in mammary glands.
source: We, therefore, used carmine alum staining and hematoxylin-eosin staining to assess the gross morphology and mammary fat pad filling of nulliparous, pregnant, and lactating females (Figure 6C). No anomalies in mammary gland morphogenesis were detected, with all genotypes exhibiting similar epithelial branch length and number, fat pad filling, alveolar size, and alveolar wall thickness.
evidence: Demonstrated through histological analysis of mammary glands.

claim: Homogenization of either the Rps27 or Rps27l locus has no effect on overall mouse fitness.
source: From this evidence, we conclude that homogenization of either the Rps27 or Rps27l locus has no effect on overall mouse fitness and also no effect on the morphology or function of tissues that preferentially express either Rps27 or Rps27l.
evidence: Inferred from the comprehensive characterization showing no detectable phenotypes.

claim: Homogenization of either the Rps27 or Rps27l locus has no effect on the morphology or function of tissues that preferentially express either Rps27 or Rps27l.
source: From this evidence, we conclude that homogenization of either the Rps27 or Rps27l locus has no effect on overall mouse fitness and also no effect on the morphology or function of tissues that preferentially express either Rps27 or Rps27l.
evidence: Inferred from the comprehensive characterization showing no detectable phenotypes in mammary gland, liver, and hematopoietic tissues.

claim: The Rps27 and Rps27l proteins are functionally similar in the setting of normal organism physiology, even in tissues that preferentially express one paralog.
source: These findings suggest that the Rps27 and Rps27l proteins are functionally similar in the setting of normal organism physiology, even in tissues that preferentially express one paralog.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of phenotypes in homogenized mice across all examined tissues.

claim: No clinically significant differences were observed between genotypes in bloodwork assays of 9-10-month-old homogenized mice.
source: At that time, we weighed the mice and performed a complete blood count and liver panel, again targeting the organ systems with preferential Rps27 or Rps27l expression. No clinically significant differences were observed between genotypes in any of the included assays (Figure 7A, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: Demonstrated through bloodwork analysis of aged mice.

claim: Homogenization of Rps27 or Rps27l has no detectable effect on the physiology of liver and hematopoietic organs, even later in life.
source: Thus, homogenization of Rps27 or Rps27l has no detectable effect on the physiology of these organs, even later in life.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of differences in bloodwork of 9-10-month-old mice.

claim: MEFs of all genotypes had similar frequency in each cell cycle phase.
source: We first analyzed their distribution across cell cycle phases when cultured in vitro and found that MEFs of all genotypes had similar frequency in each phase (Figure 7B).
evidence: Demonstrated through EdU/DAPI flow cytometry analysis.

claim: The same degree of effect from doxorubicin and etoposide treatment was seen across all genotypes of MEFs.
source: Higher doses of doxorubicin and etoposide consistently resulted in decreased cell viability, yet the same degree of effect was seen across all genotypes.
evidence: Demonstrated through cell viability assays after drug treatment.

claim: For the purposes of cellular survival and proliferation under doxorubicin or etoposide treatment, the Rps27 and Rps27l proteins appear to be interchangeable.
source: Thus, for the purposes of cellular survival and proliferation under doxorubicin or etoposide treatment, the Rps27 and Rps27l proteins also appear to be interchangeable.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of differences in cell viability between genotypes after drug treatment.

claim: At least one WGD occurred in a common ancestor of all vertebrates (1R).
source: Interestingly, it has long been hypothesized that at least one WGD occurred in a common ancestor of all vertebrates ('1R'), followed closely by either a second WGD ('2R') with subsequent loss of many duplicates or by several large segmental duplications (Dehal and Boore, 2005; Nakatani et al., 2021; Ohno, 1970; Sacerdot et al., 2018; Simakov et al., 2020; Smith et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Dehal and Boore, 2005; Nakatani et al., 2021; Ohno, 1970; Sacerdot et al., 2018; Simakov et al., 2020; Smith et al., 2018).

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are consistently identified among the 'ohnolog' gene duplicates in systematic efforts to map 1R/2R remnants throughout vertebrate genomes.
source: Indeed, in systematic efforts to map 1R/2R remnants throughout vertebrate genomes based on phylogeny and large-scale synteny (Makino and McLysaght, 2010; Sacerdot et al., 2018; Singh and Isambert, 2020), Rps27 and Rps27l are consistently identified among the 'ohnolog' gene duplicates that still comprise 25–35% of present-day vertebrate genes.
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Makino and McLysaght, 2010; Sacerdot et al., 2018; Singh and Isambert, 2020).

claim: Ohnolog gene duplicates still comprise 25-35% of present-day vertebrate genes.
source: Indeed, in systematic efforts to map 1R/2R remnants throughout vertebrate genomes based on phylogeny and large-scale synteny (Makino and McLysaght, 2010; Sacerdot et al., 2018; Singh and Isambert, 2020), Rps27 and Rps27l are consistently identified among the 'ohnolog' gene duplicates that still comprise 25–35% of present-day vertebrate genes.
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Makino and McLysaght, 2010; Sacerdot et al., 2018; Singh and Isambert, 2020).

claim: A third WGD occurred in the common ancestor to teleost fish.
source: Furthermore, a third WGD occurred in the common ancestor to teleost fish.
evidence: Established knowledge in evolutionary biology.

claim: Carp and salmon have each experienced an independent fourth WGD.
source: Carp and salmon, which each have six Rps27 paralogs, have each experienced an independent fourth WGD (Macqueen and Johnston, 2014; Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Macqueen and Johnston, 2014; Xu et al., 2019).

claim: Increases in the number of Rps27 paralogs coincide in evolutionary timing with WGDs.
source: Thus, increases in the number of Rps27 paralogs coincide in evolutionary timing with WGDs.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between WGD events and Rps27 paralog numbers across species.

claim: In fungi, genes encoding protein complexes such as the ribosome often remain duplicated after WGD but rarely duplicate on an individual basis.
source: It is important to note that the properties of Rps27 and Rps27l observed here do not necessarily extend to all mammalian RP paralogs, and that some mammalian RP paralog pairs, such as Rpl3/Rpl3l and Rpl22/Rpl22l (eL22/eL22L), have more differences in amino acid sequence than Rps27/Rps27l.
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Papp et al., 2003; Wapinski et al., 2007).

claim: Most RPs in present-day mammalian genomes are encoded by a single gene.
source: Notably, most RPs in present-day mammalian genomes are encoded by a single gene; there are only 10 known human RP paralog pairs, several of which have hallmarks of tandem duplication or retrotransposition rather than WGD (Gupta and Warner, 2014).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Gupta and Warner, 2014).

claim: There are only 10 known human RP paralog pairs.
source: Notably, most RPs in present-day mammalian genomes are encoded by a single gene; there are only 10 known human RP paralog pairs, several of which have hallmarks of tandem duplication or retrotransposition rather than WGD (Gupta and Warner, 2014).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Gupta and Warner, 2014).

claim: In teleost fish species that underwent 3R and 4R WGD, more than four Rps27 copies have been reported.
source: A final curious observation that we (Figure 1B) and others have made is that, in teleost fish species that underwent 3R and 4R WGD, more than four Rps27 copies have been reported, whereas most other RPs have reverted to fewer copies (Kuang et al., 2020; Manchado et al., 2007).
evidence: Observed in this study and cited from previous literature (Kuang et al., 2020; Manchado et al., 2007).

claim: Most other RPs in teleost fish have reverted to fewer copies after 3R and 4R WGD.
source: A final curious observation that we (Figure 1B) and others have made is that, in teleost fish species that underwent 3R and 4R WGD, more than four Rps27 copies have been reported, whereas most other RPs have reverted to fewer copies (Kuang et al., 2020; Manchado et al., 2007).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Kuang et al., 2020; Manchado et al., 2007).

claim: Each ribosome consists of 80 ribosomal proteins (RPs) and 4 ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs) in mammals.
source: In mammals, each ribosome consists of 80 ribosomal proteins (RPs) and 4 ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs), which together form a 40S small subunit and a 60S large subunit that join during translation (Anger et al., 2013; Uechi et al., 2001).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Anger et al., 2013; Uechi et al., 2001).

claim: Ten RP genes are known to exist as paralog pairs in the human genome.
source: Ten of these RP genes are known to exist as paralog pairs in the human genome, several of which are conserved among other mammals (Balasubramanian et al., 2009; Gupta and Warner, 2014; Nakao et al., 2004; Sugihara et al., 2010).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Balasubramanian et al., 2009; Gupta and Warner, 2014; Nakao et al., 2004; Sugihara et al., 2010).

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are located on separate chromosomes in human and mouse.
source: In human and mouse, Rps27 and Rps27l are located on separate chromosomes.
evidence: Established genomic information.

claim: The canonical transcripts for Rps27 and Rps27l each contain three introns.
source: Unlike the approximately 2000 mostly intronless processed RP pseudogenes resulting from retrotransposition in these genomes (Balasubramanian et al., 2009), the canonical transcripts for Rps27 and Rps27l each contain three introns and their exon junctions correspond to similar positions within the encoded proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Determined through analysis of gene structure.

claim: The exon junctions of Rps27 and Rps27l correspond to similar positions within the encoded proteins.
source: Unlike the approximately 2000 mostly intronless processed RP pseudogenes resulting from retrotransposition in these genomes (Balasubramanian et al., 2009), the canonical transcripts for Rps27 and Rps27l each contain three introns and their exon junctions correspond to similar positions within the encoded proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Determined through analysis of gene structure.

claim: There are approximately 2000 mostly intronless processed RP pseudogenes resulting from retrotransposition in human and mouse genomes.
source: Unlike the approximately 2000 mostly intronless processed RP pseudogenes resulting from retrotransposition in these genomes (Balasubramanian et al., 2009), the canonical transcripts for Rps27 and Rps27l each contain three introns and their exon junctions correspond to similar positions within the encoded proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Balasubramanian et al., 2009).

claim: In a phylogenetic tree constructed from the coding sequences of Rps27 and Rps27l across species, the Rps27 sequences from mammals and coelacanth formed a distinct clade from the corresponding Rps27l sequences.
source: Additionally, in a phylogenetic tree constructed from the coding sequences of Rps27 and Rps27l across species, the Rps27 sequences from mammals and coelacanth formed a distinct clade from the corresponding Rps27l sequences (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that duplication and subsequent divergence of these loci began in a common ancestor of these species.
evidence: Demonstrated through phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Duplication and subsequent divergence of Rps27 and Rps27l began in a common ancestor of mammals and coelacanth.
source: Additionally, in a phylogenetic tree constructed from the coding sequences of Rps27 and Rps27l across species, the Rps27 sequences from mammals and coelacanth formed a distinct clade from the corresponding Rps27l sequences (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that duplication and subsequent divergence of these loci began in a common ancestor of these species.
evidence: Inferred from phylogenetic tree topology.

claim: Transcript abundance among the core RP genes is highly correlated across cell types.
source: However, transcript abundance among the core RP genes is highly correlated across cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), which is consistent with the theory that components of a protein complex must have balanced expression for effective assembly (Guimaraes and Zavolan, 2016; Papp et al., 2003).
evidence: Demonstrated through correlation analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Components of a protein complex must have balanced expression for effective assembly.
source: However, transcript abundance among the core RP genes is highly correlated across cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), which is consistent with the theory that components of a protein complex must have balanced expression for effective assembly (Guimaraes and Zavolan, 2016; Papp et al., 2003).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Guimaraes and Zavolan, 2016; Papp et al., 2003).

claim: Mammary alveolar cells are a transient cell type that arise rapidly from luminal progenitor cells in female mammary glands during pregnancy and lactation to secrete milk components.
source: Mammary alveolar cells are a transient cell type that arise rapidly from luminal progenitor cells in female mammary glands during pregnancy and lactation to secrete milk components (Macias and Hinck, 2012).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Macias and Hinck, 2012).

claim: Rps27l expression correlates more strongly with milk protein transcripts than almost all other transcripts in the transcriptome.
source: Indeed, these transcripts correlated more strongly with Rps27l expression than almost all others in the transcriptome (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Determined through correlation analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Among differentiated mammary alveolar cells, Rps27l expression is inversely correlated with mRNA abundance of other Trp53-upregulated genes.
source: Among differentiated mammary alveolar cells, we found that Rps27l expression is inversely correlated with mRNA abundance of other Trp53-upregulated genes, suggesting that single cells with high Rps27l expression do not have increased Trp53 activity.
evidence: Demonstrated through correlation analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Single cells with high Rps27l expression do not have increased Trp53 activity.
source: Among differentiated mammary alveolar cells, we found that Rps27l expression is inversely correlated with mRNA abundance of other Trp53-upregulated genes, suggesting that single cells with high Rps27l expression do not have increased Trp53 activity.
evidence: Inferred from the inverse correlation between Rps27l and other Trp53 targets.

claim: A ribosome does not simultaneously contain Rps27 and Rps27l.
source: Minimal Rps27 is detected when targeting Rps27l for pulldown and vice versa, confirming that a ribosome does not simultaneously contain Rps27 and Rps27l and that we did not isolate undigested polysomes containing multiple ribosomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated through FLAG-IP western blot showing minimal cross-detection.

claim: The total RPFs from Rps27-FLAG and Rps27l-FLAG cell lines did not contain mRNAs that differed significantly in abundance compared to wild-type control.
source: The total RPFs from the two FLAG-tagged cell lines did not contain mRNAs that differed significantly in abundance either in comparison between the Rps27-FLAG line and Rps27l-FLAG line or in comparison to a passage-matched wild-type (WT) control line (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Demonstrated through ribosome profiling analysis.

claim: FLAG-tagging did not alter the landscape of normally translated mRNAs.
source: This confirms that FLAG-tagging did not alter the landscape of normally translated mRNAs.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of differences in total RPFs between FLAG-tagged and wild-type cells.

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l loss-of-function alleles are each lethal in homozygosity, even with both alleles of the other paralog intact.
source: The fact that Rps27 and Rps27l loss-of-function alleles are each lethal in homozygosity, even with both alleles of the other paralog intact, disfavors the hypothesis that Rps27 and Rps27l engage in paralog buffering.
evidence: Demonstrated through breeding experiments showing lethality of homozygous knockouts.

claim: The hypothesis that Rps27 and Rps27l engage in paralog buffering is disfavored.
source: The fact that Rps27 and Rps27l loss-of-function alleles are each lethal in homozygosity, even with both alleles of the other paralog intact, disfavors the hypothesis that Rps27 and Rps27l engage in paralog buffering.
evidence: Inferred from the inability of one paralog to compensate for loss of the other.

claim: Impaired ribosome biogenesis due to perturbed dosage balance of RPs activates Trp53 via nucleolar stress or translation inhibition.
source: However, the study of Rps27 and Rps27l is complicated by the consideration that impaired ribosome biogenesis due to perturbed dosage balance of other RPs has also been shown to activate Trp53 via nucleolar stress or translation inhibition (Nicolas et al., 2016; Russo and Russo, 2017; Zhang and Lu, 2009).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Nicolas et al., 2016; Russo and Russo, 2017; Zhang and Lu, 2009).

claim: Depletion of an RP gene is associated with increased expression of a paralogous gene in some instances.
source: Interestingly, we observed that Rps27lexon2del / + and Rps27lexon2del / exon2del tissues had increased expression of the intact Rps27 protein, which is analogous to previously reported instances in which depletion of an RP gene is associated with increased expression of a paralogous gene (Milenkovic et al., 2023; O'Leary et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Milenkovic et al., 2023; O'Leary et al., 2013).

claim: Rps27 protein has a critical function in very early developmental processes.
source: The difference in the timing of lethality could be consistent with the two proteins having distinct functions; under such a model, it would appear that Rps27 protein has a critical function in very early developmental processes, while the functions of Rps27l protein are dispensable until postnatal stages.
evidence: Inferred from the early embryonic lethality of Rps27 knockout, though the authors note this is one possible interpretation.

claim: The functions of Rps27l protein are dispensable until postnatal stages.
source: The difference in the timing of lethality could be consistent with the two proteins having distinct functions; under such a model, it would appear that Rps27 protein has a critical function in very early developmental processes, while the functions of Rps27l protein are dispensable until postnatal stages.
evidence: Inferred from the postnatal lethality of Rps27l knockout, though the authors note this is one possible interpretation.

claim: Rps27l depletion impairs ribosome biogenesis and causes accumulation of unincorporated RPs, which increase Trp53 activity by blocking its degradation by Mdm2.
source: This finding was attributed to a model in which Rps27l depletion impairs ribosome biogenesis and thus causes accumulation of unincorporated RPs, which increase Trp53 activity by blocking its degradation by Mdm2.
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Xiong et al., 2014).

claim: Increased Trp53 from Rps27l depletion triggers apoptosis in hematopoietic tissues.
source: The increased Trp53 triggers apoptosis in hematopoietic tissues (Xiong et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Xiong et al., 2014).

claim: Purified Rps27 and Rps27l protein bind the Trp53 ubiquitin ligase Mdm2 in vitro with different affinity.
source: Purified Rps27 and Rps27l protein bind the Trp53 ubiquitin ligase Mdm2 in vitro with different affinity and are degraded by Mdm2 at different rates, which depends on the N-terminal portion of Rps27 and Rps27l where the differing residues reside (Xiong et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Rps27 and Rps27l are degraded by Mdm2 at different rates.

evidence: Cited from previous literature (Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: The differential degradation of Rps27 and Rps27l by Mdm2 depends on the N-terminal portion where the differing residues reside.

evidence: Cited from previous literature (Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Knockdown of Rps27l but not Rps27 reduces the levels of DNA repair proteins FANCD2 and FANCI.
source: Also, knockdown of Rps27l but not Rps27 was reported to reduce the levels of DNA repair proteins FANCD2 and FANCI (Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from previous literature (Sun et al., 2020).

claim: Total expression of Rps27 and Rps27l impacts in vivo fitness more so than differences in protein characteristics.
source: Nevertheless, the normal physiology of both homogenized mouse lines until at least 9–10 months of age suggests that total expression of Rps27 and Rps27l impacts in vivo fitness more so than differences in protein characteristics.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of phenotypes in homogenized mice despite protein sequence differences.

claim: Gene duplication is a fundamental evolutionary process that expands the complexity and functional repertoire of genomes.
